required.fact: Problem: existing RAG relies on flat data representations and lacks contextual awareness, giving fragmented answers
required.evidence: existing RAG systems have significant limitations, including reliance on flat data representations and inadequate contextual awareness

required.fact: Method: LightRAG incorporates graph structures into text indexing and retrieval
required.evidence: we propose LightRAG, which incorporates graph structures into text indexing and retrieval processes

required.fact: Core: dual-level retrieval, low-level (entities, relations) and high-level (topics, themes)
Incremental update without rebuilding the whole index
required.evidence: an incremental update algorithm that ensures the timely integration of new data

required.fact: Result: improvements in retrieval accuracy and efficiency over existing approaches
required.evidence: Extensive experimental validation demonstrates considerable improvements in retrieval accuracy and efficiency

bonus.fact: Graph structures combined with vector representations
bonus.evidence: the integration of graph structures with vector representations

bonus.fact: Four datasets (Agriculture, CS, Legal, Mix) and four dimensions (Comprehensiveness, Diversity, Empowerment, Overall)
Retrieval cost: LightRAG under 100 tokens and 1 API call vs GraphRAG about 610,000 tokens
bonus.evidence: using fewer than 100 tokens for keyword generation and retrieval, requiring only a single API call
We have made our LightRAG open-source

bonus.fact: Three challenges: comprehensive retrieval, retrieval efficiency, rapid adaptation to new data

required.fact: Both graph-based; LightRAG outperforms GraphRAG, especially on the larger Agriculture, CS and Legal datasets

required.fact: LightRAG's clearest advantage is Diversity, attributed to dual-level retrieval
required.evidence: LightRAG demonstrates a significant advantage in the Diversity metric

required.fact: Retrieval cost: GraphRAG 1,399 communities, 610 level-2 used, ~1,000 tokens each, ~610,000 tokens, hundreds of API calls; LightRAG under 100 tokens, one API call
Incremental update: GraphRAG dismantles and regenerates communities, about 1,399 x 2 x 5,000 tokens; LightRAG integrates new entities and relations without full reconstruction
required.evidence: GraphRAG must dismantle its existing community structure

required.fact: Mechanism: GraphRAG traverses community reports (brute-force); LightRAG uses dual-level retrieval over graph and vector representations
required.evidence: existing methods often rely on brute-force searches for each generated community

required.fact: -Low: advantage in comprehensiveness, less depth on specific entities

required.fact: -Origin: no significant decline; improvements on Agriculture and Mix; graph indexing already captured key information, original text adds noise
required.evidence: does not exhibit significant performance declines across all four datasets
